messages:
emily-cs: FYI incoming escalation from ACME — ~120 users lost the 'engineer' product role after last Okta group sync. Customer says no manual changes on their side.
navin-sre: Oof. Any error codes or SCIM audit events?
emily-cs: They forwarded SCIM logs. Most PATCH /Users responses were 200 but members arrays ended up empty for specific groups. Also saw duplicate group externalIds in a short window.
jason-se: Can you paste the raw SCIM event for one of the affected groups?
emily-cs: Sure — here's the relevant part they sent (redacted):
```
PATCH /Groups/urn:scim:group:extid:acme|eng|2026
Body: { "members": [{ "value": "user-123" }, { "value": "user-456" }] }
Response 200 OK
Later GET /Groups?filter=externalId eq "acme|eng"
Returned two groups: externalId="acme|eng" and externalId="acme" with local name "eng" (normalized)
```
navin-sre: Hmm. That pipe character in externalId is suspicious. Our group normalizer strips delimiters in some older mapper configs to create a stable shortname. If Okta started sending a different externalId format (e.g., they introduced suffixes), we could be collapsing distinct groups into one or splitting one into two.
kai-platform: Adding context: a week ago a change was deployed to the SCIM mapping that normalizes group displayName -> role name by replacing non-alphanum with dash. It also tried to canonicalize externalId by splitting on delimiters `[-_,|:]` and using the first token. That could cause collisions if Okta uses compound externalIds.
sam-support: Customer says they recently switched to Okta inline group push from a third-party rule that appended a timestamp token with `|` — so externalId changed from `acme|eng` to `acme|eng|ts`.
maria-cs: So the mapper took the first token (`acme`) as canonical externalId and assigned roles based on that? That would map all acme* groups together, and then some groups had members overwritten by later patches.
okta-sync-bot: SYSTEM: sync job 2026-05-04T14:02:11Z finished for org acme (push). 102 group PATCH events, 9 duplicate externalId warnings.
jason-se: Any sign of our deprovisioning job running after the bad mapping? If group-members are overwritten to empty, that could have triggered deprovisioning flows removing roles.
emily-cs: Yes — timeline from customer: Okta push -> group normalization collapse -> later background reconcile job detected missing members and ran deprovisioning for role 'engineer'. They only noticed when users lost product access.
navin-sre: Repro steps I want to run: 1) simulate Okta push with compound externalId `acme|eng|202604` 2) hit our SCIM /Groups PATCH 3) check what our mapper writes into DB and whether normalizeExternalId() returns first token only 4) run reconcile job locally.
jason-se: Throwing a quick curl for repro:
```
curl -X PATCH "$SCIM_URL/Groups/urn:scim:group:extid:acme|eng|202604" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "members": [{"value":"user-1"}, {"value":"user-2"}] }'
```
kai-platform: If that reproduces, we should patch mapper to use full externalId (no tokenization) and make normalization configurable per-connector. Also add a safelist for connectors that send compound IDs.
oncall-ops: ETA for mitigation? Customer is P0.
sam-support: Short-term mitigation: disable reconcile job for the org acme (flag) and run a manual resync reading externalId raw values, then restore memberships from our SCIM audit logs. I can start the flag if we agree.
emily-cs: Customer agreed to a planned manual resync. They want a rollback if possible.
maria-cs: I'll coordinate the resync and message the customer with the window.
navin-sre: Action items: 1) kai -> quick config change to stop tokenization for Okta connector + patch to use full externalId (PR) 2) sam/support -> pause reconcile for acme and start manual resync using audit snapshot 3) jason -> add safety guard so reconcile doesn't auto-deprovision when >1 group externalId collision seen in last 24h 4) emily/maria -> customer comms and scheduled resync.
kai-platform: I'll open a small PR today to flip the flag and add a migration to remap existing group keys to full externalId. Risk low.
sam-support: I've toggled org flag to pause auto-deprovision for acme. Confirmed via admin console.
emily-cs: Customer on call at 17:30 UTC for resync. Can we have a brief playbook in the thread for the manual steps?
jason-se: Manual resync playbook (short):
1) export group membership audit snapshot for acme (last good state)
2) map snapshot members -> full externalId values from incoming Okta payloads
3) run bulk PATCH to restore members for affected groups (use dry-run first)
4) verify role assignments in product (smoke test with 3 sample users)
5) unpause reconcile and monitor 1h

Include command examples and one-liners in the runbook.
maria-cs: Thanks — sending customer the time and runbook now. They asked if we can prevent this for other customers.
kai-platform: I'll follow up with a roadmap ticket to make connector normalization explicit per-connector and add a warning/error if normalization would cause collisions.
oncall-ops: Please update incident tracker with the flag toggle and PR link.
emily-cs: Will do. Thank you all. :heart:
sam-support: After resync we'll run a postmortem to update docs and add a regression test to the SCIM e2e suite. :thumbsup:
